lesson_title: The Nine Learners Who Got Counted Twice
hook_text: 22 play soccer. 15 play chess. Add them: 37. But only 28 kids are standing in the hoops. Who are the phantom nine?
clip_script: Chalk a rectangle on the playground — all 40 learners inside. Two overlapping hoops: soccer left, chess right. The principal wants to know how many play at least one game. A helper adds the clipboards: 22 soccer names plus 15 chess names — 37. But count the bodies standing in hoops: only 28. Where did nine people go? Walk to the lens where the hoops overlap. Nine learners stand there — and each one is written on BOTH clipboards. One person, two entries. The addition greeted them twice. The repair is one clean move: subtract the shared members once. Thirty-seven minus nine — 28, matching the ground exactly. That is the addition rule: P of A or B equals P of A plus P of B, minus P of A and B. The subtraction is not decoration. It is the arithmetic refusing to count anybody twice.
visual_style: Top-down playground animation: chalk rectangle, two neon hoops sliding into overlap, name tags flying from two clipboards onto learners, the nine overlap learners flashing double tags, then nine tags dissolving as the count corrects from 37 to 28.
pacing: Brisk setup, puzzled pause on the 37-versus-28 clash, slow zoom into the lens for the reveal, punchy one-line rule to close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to master Venn diagrams and the addition rule.
